title: Authorizing shipment views, assignments, and carrier status updates
name: Shipment status routes

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how these routes check whether the caller may read or change a shipment? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The status route checks that the caller is a carrier but never checks that this carrier is the one assigned to the shipment (shipment.carrierId === principal.orgId), unlike canSee in the GET route. Any carrier can mark another carrier's shipment as delivered or exception just by knowing its ID, which corrupts tracking and can trigger payouts or customer notifications.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A dispatcher from org A calls GET /shipments/:id for a shipment created by org B. What is the response?
choices: 200 with the shipment, since dispatchers can see all shipments
choiceQuestions.explanation: canSee returns s.shipperOrgId === p.orgId for dispatchers, which is false here, and the route answers 404 just as it does for a missing shipment, so the shipment's existence is not revealed. The caller is authenticated, so not 401, and the route never returns 403 for a visibility failure.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two requests from the assigned carrier try to move the same in_transit shipment, one to out_for_delivery and one to exception, at the same moment. What happens?
choices: Both succeed and the last write wins
One succeeds; the other gets 409 concurrent_update because updateStatus is conditional on the version both requests read
The second request waits for a row lock and then applies on top of the first
choiceQuestions.explanation: Both read version N and both transitions are allowed from in_transit. updateStatus only applies when the stored version still equals N, so the first write bumps the version and the second gets null, which the route turns into 409 concurrent_update. There is no last-write-wins and no blocking row lock.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A carrier tries to move a shipment from created straight to in_transit. What happens?
choices: It succeeds, because in_transit is a valid carrier status
409 invalid_transition, because created has no carrier transitions
403 forbidden, because only dispatchers can update created shipments
400, because the request body is invalid
choiceQuestions.explanation: CARRIER_TRANSITIONS.created is an empty list, so allowed.includes("in_transit") is false and the route returns 409 with from and to. The role check passes for a carrier, and the body has a status, so it is neither 403 nor 400.
